findings.title: Credentials sent in cleartext over HTTP Basic Auth
findings.description: Login credentials or secrets were transmitted without encryption over HTTP Basic Auth. Anyone able to observe this traffic (on the same network, a compromised switch, or a man-in-the-middle position) can capture and reuse them. Observed: "credentials: admin:SuperSecret123".
findings.remediation: Disable HTTP Basic Auth or wrap it in TLS (e.g. FTPS/FTP-over-TLS, IMAPS/POP3S/SMTPS, SSH instead of Telnet). Rotate any exposed credentials immediately.
findings.mitre: T1040 Network Sniffing / T1552 Unsecured Credentials

findings.title: Credentials sent in cleartext over Telnet
findings.description: Login credentials or secrets were transmitted without encryption over Telnet. Anyone able to observe this traffic (on the same network, a compromised switch, or a man-in-the-middle position) can capture and reuse them. Observed: "login:", "admin..", "Password:".
findings.remediation: Disable Telnet or wrap it in TLS (e.g. FTPS/FTP-over-TLS, IMAPS/POP3S/SMTPS, SSH instead of Telnet). Rotate any exposed credentials immediately.
findings.mitre: T1040 Network Sniffing / T1552 Unsecured Credentials

findings.title: Possible ARP spoofing: 192.168.1.1 claimed by multiple MACs
findings.description: The IP address 192.168.1.1 was announced by 2 different MAC addresses (00:11:22:33:44:01, de:ad:be:ef:00:99). This is the signature of an ARP cache poisoning / man-in-the-middle attack, where an attacker impersonates another host (often the gateway) to intercept traffic.
findings.remediation: Identify which MAC is legitimate for this IP. Enable Dynamic ARP Inspection (DAI) and DHCP snooping on managed switches, use static ARP entries for critical hosts (e.g. the gateway), and isolate the offending device.

findings.title: Multiple DHCP servers detected (possible rogue DHCP)
findings.description: DHCP offers/acks came from 2 distinct servers (192.168.1.1, 192.168.1.66). A rogue DHCP server can hand out a malicious gateway or DNS server to redirect and intercept traffic.
findings.remediation: Confirm which DHCP server is authorized. Enable DHCP snooping on switches to permit DHCP replies only from trusted ports, and locate/remove the rogue server.

findings.title: Obsolete TLS version or weak cipher suites negotiated
findings.description: TLS handshakes used deprecated protocol versions (TLS 1.0) or weak cipher suites (TLS_RSA_WITH_RC4_128_SHA, TLS_RSA_WITH_3DES_EDE_CBC_SHA). These are vulnerable to known attacks (BEAST, POODLE, RC4 biases) and can be downgraded or decrypted.
findings.remediation: Require TLS 1.2 or 1.3 and disable SSLv3/TLS 1.0/1.1. Remove RC4, 3DES, EXPORT, and NULL cipher suites; prefer AEAD suites (AES-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305).

findings.title: Possible DNS tunneling to evil-c2.com
findings.description: 30 unique, long (avg 47 chars), high-entropy subdomains were queried under evil-c2.com with heavy TXT/NULL record use. This pattern is characteristic of DNS tunneling — encoding data (exfiltration or command & control) inside DNS queries to bypass firewalls. e.g. upi6rlqkhzvlmmcfabngr84jjpm6lerd5x4mw1xb.tunnel.evil-c2.com
findings.remediation: Block or sinkhole evil-c2.com. Inspect the querying host for malware/beaconing, restrict outbound DNS to approved resolvers, and deploy DNS monitoring that flags high query volume, long labels, and unusual record types.
findings.mitre: T1071.004 Application Layer Protocol: DNS / T1048 Exfiltration

findings.title: TCP port scan from 192.168.1.66
findings.description: 192.168.1.66 sent SYN packets to 20 distinct ports on 192.168.1.1 in this capture — a hallmark of port scanning / service enumeration, typically an early reconnaissance step before an attack.
findings.remediation: Investigate the source host — if it is not an authorized scanner, treat it as potentially compromised. Restrict exposed services with a host/network firewall and enable rate-limiting or an IDS/IPS to detect scans.

findings.title: Telnet (unencrypted remote shell) observed
findings.description: Telnet (unencrypted remote shell) does not encrypt data in transit, exposing content and any credentials to eavesdropping and tampering. 5 packet(s) used this protocol.

findings.title: Unencrypted HTTP observed
findings.description: Unencrypted HTTP does not encrypt data in transit, exposing content and any credentials to eavesdropping and tampering. 2 packet(s) used this protocol.
findings.remediation: Serve the application over HTTPS (TLS 1.2+) and redirect HTTP to HTTPS with HSTS.
